1	// This file implements the organization-scoped audit chain. Every successful
2	// policy publish or rollback, and every Decide called with a non-empty
3	// decision organization, leaves an immutable record in that organization.
4	//
5	// Records carry an organization-local sequence starting at 1 and a SHA-256
6	// fingerprint that chains each record to the previous one. The genesis
7	// fingerprint binds the organization name, so records from another
8	// organization can never validate as part of this chain even when the
9	// sequence numbers and identifiers coincide.
10	package darksafe
11	
12	import (
13		"crypto/sha256"
14		"encoding/binary"
15		"encoding/hex"
16		"encoding/json"
17		"errors"
18		"fmt"
19	)
20	
21	// Audit record categories.
22	const (
23		// AuditPolicyChange is a successful publish or rollback.
24		AuditPolicyChange = "policy_change"
25		// AuditDecision is one Decide evaluation.
26		AuditDecision = "decision"
27	)
28	
29	// Sentinel errors for the audit entry points. Callers distinguish them
30	// with errors.Is; every one leaves state unchanged.
31	var (
32		// ErrInvalidPage means a page size or range argument was invalid.
33		ErrInvalidPage = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit page")
34		// ErrInvalidRange means the upper bound is beyond what exists, the
35		// range is inverted, or a supplied fingerprint does not match.
36		ErrInvalidRange = errors.New("darksafe: invalid audit range")
37		// ErrAuditNotFound means no record exists at the requested sequence.
38		ErrAuditNotFound = errors.New("darksafe: audit record not found")
39		// ErrAuditNotADecision means the record at the sequence is not a
40		// decision record and therefore cannot be rechecked.
41		ErrAuditNotADecision = errors.New("darksafe: audit record is not a decision")
42	)
43	
44	// PolicyChange captures a successful publish or rollback.
45	type PolicyChange struct {
46		// Version is the newly created policy version.
47		Version int
48		// Policies is the full policy set of the new version.
49		Policies []Policy
50		// SourceVersion is the version copied by a rollback, and 0 for an
51		// ordinary publish.
52		SourceVersion int
53		// RolledBack reports whether the change was produced by Rollback.
54		RolledBack bool
55	}
56	
57	// DecisionRecord captures one Decide call: the full request and the
58	// decision actually returned.
59	type DecisionRecord struct {
60		Request  OrgRequest
61		Decision Decision
62	}
63	
64	// AuditRecord is one immutable entry in an organization's audit chain.
65	type AuditRecord struct {
66		Org      string
67		Seq      int // organization-local, starting at 1 and gapless
68		Kind     string
69		Change   *PolicyChange   // present when Kind == AuditPolicyChange
70		Decision *DecisionRecord // present when Kind == AuditDecision
71	
72		// PrevFingerprint is the fingerprint of the preceding record, or the
73		// genesis fingerprint for the first record.
74		PrevFingerprint string
75		// Fingerprint binds this record's full content to its predecessor.
76		Fingerprint string
77	}
78	
79	// rawEnvelopePrefix opens every raw-byte canonical encoding. It never
80	// coincides with the start of a JSON envelope (always '{'), so
81	// fingerprints from the two encodings live in collision-free spaces.
82	const rawEnvelopePrefix = "darksafe-audit-raw-v1\x00"
83	
84	// fingerprintTag delimits one field or nested value within the canonical
85	// binary encoding. Distinct tags keep two payloads that merely share
86	// adjacent bytes apart (e.g. ["ab",""] vs ["a","b"]).
87	type fingerprintTag byte
88	
89	const (
90		tagEnvelope fingerprintTag = iota + 1
91		tagSeq
92		tagString
93		tagStringList
94		tagBool
95		tagPolicy
96		tagPolicyList
97		tagChange
98		tagSubject
99		tagResource
100		tagDecision
101		tagDecisionRecord
102	)
103	
104	// fingerprintEncoder builds the canonical byte representation of an
105	// envelope. Unlike encoding/json it writes string contents byte-for-byte
106	// with an explicit length prefix, so strings carrying invalid UTF-8 stay
107	// distinguishable: encoding/json renders both a raw 0xFF byte and a raw
108	// 0xFE byte as the U+FFFD replacement rune, collapsing genuinely
109	// different content onto identical fingerprints.
110	type fingerprintEncoder struct {
111		buf []byte
112	}
113	
114	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) tag(t fingerprintTag) {
115		e.buf = append(e.buf, byte(t))
116	}
117	
118	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) int64Tag(t fingerprintTag, v int64) {
119		e.tag(t)
120		var b [8]byte
121		binary.BigEndian.PutUint64(b[:], uint64(v))
122		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
123	}
124	
125	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) boolTag(t fingerprintTag, v bool) {
126		e.tag(t)
127		if v {
128			e.buf = append(e.buf, 1)
129		} else {
130			e.buf = append(e.buf, 0)
131		}
132	}
133	
134	// rawString tags and writes a string from its exact memory bytes. No
135	// validation, replacement or normalization is ever performed: an invalid
136	// UTF-8 byte reaches the hash unchanged.
137	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) rawString(s string) {
138		e.tag(tagString)
139		var b [4]byte
140		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(len(s)))
141		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
142		e.buf = append(e.buf, s...)
143	}
144	
145	// put appends one raw framing byte. It is the fingerprint sink's side of the
146	// shared list shape: the list presence marker goes into the canonical bytes
147	// verbatim.
148	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) put(b byte) {
149		e.buf = append(e.buf, b)
150	}
151	
152	// listCount writes a list element count as a big-endian uint32. The raw
153	// canonical encoding has no length ceiling beyond the hash input, so unlike
154	// the archive sink the count is written unconditionally; only the list shape
155	// (nil marker, presence marker, count then one item per element) is shared.
156	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) listCount(n int) {
157		var b [4]byte
158		binary.BigEndian.PutUint32(b[:], uint32(n))
159		e.buf = append(e.buf, b[:]...)
160	}
161	
162	// stringList preserves nil-vs-empty explicitly: in the JSON envelope a
163	// nil slice is "null" and a non-nil empty slice is "[]", so the raw
164	// encoding must keep the two shapes apart as well. The list's own kind tag
165	// leads, then the shared list shape carries the presence marker, count and
166	// elements under it.
167	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) stringList(items []string) {
168		e.tag(tagStringList)
169		writeListShape(e, items, e.rawString)
170	}
171	
172	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policy(p Policy) {
173		e.tag(tagPolicy)
174		// Field order, the Recursive boolean's position, and ResourceID being
175		// appended only when set all come from the single policy field table, so
176		// the fingerprint and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place.
177		for i := range policyFields {
178			f := &policyFields[i]
179			switch f.kind {
180			case policyFieldString:
181				e.rawString(f.getString(p))
182			case policyFieldOptionalString:
183				// ResourceID participates only when set, pairing with its
184				// omitempty JSON tag, so the legacy fingerprint bytes are
185				// unchanged for resource-unrestricted policies.
186				if v := f.getString(p); v != "" {
187					e.rawString(v)
188				}
189			case policyFieldBool:
190				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(p))
191			}
192		}
193	}
194	
195	// policyList frames the full policy set with the shared list shape, led by
196	// the policy-list tag so a policy set can never collide with a string list
197	// whose concatenated bytes happen to match.
198	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) policyList(policies []Policy) {
199		e.tag(tagPolicyList)
200		writeListShape(e, policies, e.policy)
201	}
202	
203	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) change(c *PolicyChange) {
204		e.tag(tagChange)
205		// A nil pointer is encoded as tagChange alone; a present value's
206		// fields follow immediately.
207		if c == nil {
208			return
209		}
210		// Field order comes from the single policy-change field table, so the
211		// fingerprint, the UTF-8 decision, the archive and the detaching copy
212		// enumerate fields in exactly one place. No change field is skipped.
213		for i := range changeFields {
214			f := &changeFields[i]
215			switch f.kind {
216			case changeFieldInt:
217				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(c)))
218			case changeFieldPolicyList:
219				e.policyList(f.getPolicies(c))
220			case changeFieldBool:
221				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(c))
222			}
223		}
224	}
225	
226	func (e *fingerprintEncoder) decisionRecord(d *DecisionRecord) {
227		e.tag(tagDecisionRecord)
228		if d == nil {
229			return
230		}
231		// Field order and the subject/resource/decision group markers all come
232		// from the single decision field table, so the fingerprint, the UTF-8
233		// decision and the archive enumerate fields in exactly one place. No
234		// request or decision field is skipped.
235		for i := range decisionFields {
236			f := &decisionFields[i]
237			if f.groupTag != 0 {
238				e.tag(f.groupTag)
239			}
240			switch f.kind {
241			case decisionFieldString:
242				e.rawString(f.getString(d))
243			case decisionFieldStringList:
244				e.stringList(f.getList(d))
245			case decisionFieldBool:
246				e.boolTag(tagBool, f.getBool(d))
247			case decisionFieldInt:
248				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(d)))
249			}
250		}
251	}
252	
253	// encodeCanonical returns the raw bytes fingerprinted for a record whose
254	// strings include invalid UTF-8. Every string the record carries reaches
255	// the output byte-for-byte, at whatever nesting depth or list position it
256	// occupies. The prefix separates this encoding space from JSON
257	// fingerprints. The outer fields come from the single record field table,
258	// so this encoding enumerates exactly the envelope members the JSON
259	// encoding and the valid-UTF-8 scan see, in the same order.
260	func encodeCanonical(r *AuditRecord) []byte {
261		e := &fingerprintEncoder{buf: []byte(rawEnvelopePrefix)}
262		e.tag(tagEnvelope)
263		for i := range recordFields {
264			f := &recordFields[i]
265			if f.jsonKey == "" {
266				// The record's own fingerprint is never an input to itself.
267				continue
268			}
269			switch f.kind {
270			case recordFieldString:
271				e.rawString(f.getString(r))
272			case recordFieldInt:
273				e.int64Tag(tagSeq, int64(f.getInt(r)))
274			case recordFieldChange:
275				e.change(f.getChange(r))
276			case recordFieldDecision:
277				e.decisionRecord(f.getDecision(r))
278			}
279		}
280		return e.buf
281	}
282	
283	// genesisFingerprint derives the chain root from the organization name,
284	// keeping equal identifiers in different organizations independent.
285	func genesisFingerprint(org string) string {
286		sum := sha256.Sum256([]byte("darksafe-audit-genesis\x00" + org))
287		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
288	}
289	
290	// encodeJSONEnvelope renders the fingerprint envelope of a record whose
291	// strings are all valid UTF-8 as the exact byte sequence the historical
292	// encoding/json envelope struct produced: the envelope members in the
293	// single record field table's order, every string, integer and payload
294	// encoded by encoding/json itself, and the two payload members dropped
295	// when absent exactly as their historical omitempty tags did. Walking the
296	// table keeps this object in lockstep with the raw canonical encoding, the
297	// valid-UTF-8 scan and the archive framing by construction.
298	func encodeJSONEnvelope(r *AuditRecord) []byte {
299		var buf []byte
300		buf = append(buf, '{')
301		first := true
302		for i := range recordFields {
303			f := &recordFields[i]
304			if f.jsonKey == "" {
305				// The record's own fingerprint is never an input to itself.
306				continue
307			}
308			var (
309				value []byte
310				err   error
311			)
312			switch f.kind {
313			case recordFieldString:
314				value, err = json.Marshal(f.getString(r))
315			case recordFieldInt:
316				value, err = json.Marshal(f.getInt(r))
317			case recordFieldChange:
318				c := f.getChange(r)
319				if c == nil {
320					continue
321				}
322				value, err = json.Marshal(c)
323			case recordFieldDecision:
324				d := f.getDecision(r)
325				if d == nil {
326					continue
327				}
328				value, err = json.Marshal(d)
329			}
330			if err != nil {
331				// All envelope values are plain, JSON-encodable values; a
332				// failure here indicates a programming error, not user input.
333				panic(fmt.Errorf("darksafe: audit envelope must encode: %w", err))
334			}
335			if !first {
336				buf = append(buf, ',')
337			}
338			first = false
339			buf = append(buf, '"')
340			buf = append(buf, f.jsonKey...)
341			buf = append(buf, '"', ':')
342			buf = append(buf, value...)
343		}
344		return append(buf, '}')
345	}
346	
347	// fingerprintFor returns the fingerprint for a record. Records made
348	// exclusively of valid UTF-8 keep the historical JSON fingerprint, so old
349	// exports and checkpoints remain valid; records containing invalid bytes
350	// use the length-prefixed raw encoding that protects their exact bytes.
351	// Both families cover exactly the envelope members of the single record
352	// field table — never the record's own fingerprint.
353	func fingerprintFor(r *AuditRecord) string {
354		if recordUsesRawBytes(r) {
355			sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeCanonical(r))
356			return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
357		}
358		sum := sha256.Sum256(encodeJSONEnvelope(r))
359		return hex.EncodeToString(sum[:])
360	}

362	// clonePolicies returns a detached copy of a policy set.
363	func clonePolicies(in []Policy) []Policy {
364		if in == nil {
365			return nil
366		}
367		return append([]Policy(nil), in...)
368	}
369	
370	// cloneChange returns a detached copy of a policy-change payload.
371	func cloneChange(c *PolicyChange) *PolicyChange {
372		if c == nil {
373			return nil
374		}
375		cp := *c
376		// Detach every list the single policy-change field table carries; the
377		// per-list nil-versus-empty handling stays exactly as clonePolicies
378		// defines it.
379		cloneChangeLists(&cp, c)
380		return &cp
381	}
382	
383	// cloneStrings returns a detached copy of a string slice while preserving
384	// its nil-versus-empty shape: a nil slice stays nil, and every non-nil
385	// slice, including a non-nil empty slice that still carries spare capacity,
386	// receives its own backing array. Copying only when len > 0 is not enough:
387	// a caller may submit make([]string, 0, 4), and aliasing that array into a
388	// stored record would let an append to one handed-out copy overwrite the
389	// first element of every other copy that shares it.
390	func cloneStrings(in []string) []string {
391		if in == nil {
392			return nil
393		}
394		return append([]string{}, in...)
395	}
396	
397	// cloneDecision returns a detached copy of a decision payload.
398	func cloneDecision(d *DecisionRecord) *DecisionRecord {
399		if d == nil {
400			return nil
401		}
402		cp := *d
403		// Detach every list the single decision field table carries, on non-nil
404		// rather than on len > 0 so empty-but-capacious lists are independent
405		// copies too; nil lists stay nil.
406		cloneDecisionLists(&cp, d)
407		return &cp
408	}
409	
410	// cloneRecord returns a fully detached copy of a record.
411	func cloneRecord(r *AuditRecord) *AuditRecord {
412		cp := *r
413		cp.Change = cloneChange(r.Change)
414		cp.Decision = cloneDecision(r.Decision)
415		return &cp
416	}

418	// appendAuditLocked validates, fingerprints and stores one record. It runs
419	// under the store mutex and is the single place records are created.
420	func (st *orgState) appendAuditLocked(org, kind string, change *PolicyChange, decision *DecisionRecord) *AuditRecord {
421		seq := len(st.audit) + 1
422		prev := genesisFingerprint(org)
423		if len(st.audit) > 0 {
424			prev = st.audit[len(st.audit)-1].Fingerprint
425		}
426		// Store detached copies; later caller mutation must not reach the chain.
427		rec := &AuditRecord{
428			Org:             org,
429			Seq:             seq,
430			Kind:            kind,
431			Change:          cloneChange(change),
432			Decision:        cloneDecision(decision),
433			PrevFingerprint: prev,
434		}
435		rec.Fingerprint = fingerprintFor(rec)
436		st.audit = append(st.audit, rec)
437		return cloneRecord(rec)
438	}
439	
440	// auditHeadLocked returns the highest sequence in the chain and the
441	// fingerprint that covers it: (0, genesis) for an organization with no
442	// records.
443	func (st *orgState) auditHeadLocked(org string) (int, string) {
444		if len(st.audit) == 0 {
445			return 0, genesisFingerprint(org)
446		}
447		last := st.audit[len(st.audit)-1]
448		return last.Seq, last.Fingerprint
449	}

451	// Checkpoint pins an audit query to an exact point in a chain.
452	type Checkpoint struct {
453		Org         string
454		EndSeq      int
455		Fingerprint string
456	}
457	
458	// AuditPage is one stable slice of an organization's audit chain.
459	type AuditPage struct {
460		Org     string
461		Records []AuditRecord
462		// BeginSeq/EndSeq delimit the whole pinned range, not just this page.
463		BeginSeq int
464		EndSeq   int
465		// Next is the first sequence of the following page, 0 when exhausted.
466		Next int
467		// Checkpoint is the pinned upper bound shared by every page.
468		Checkpoint Checkpoint
469	}
470	
471	// recordMatches reports whether a record survives the query filters. Every
472	// set filter is a conjunction: kind, subject and resource conditions must
473	// all hold. Empty filter values mean "not set".
474	func recordMatches(r *AuditRecord, kind, subjectID, resourceID string) bool {
475		if kind != "" && r.Kind != kind {
476			return false
477		}
478		if subjectID != "" {
479			// A subject filter selects decision records of that subject only.
480			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
481				r.Decision.Request.Subject.ID != subjectID {
482				return false
483			}
484		}
485		if resourceID != "" {
486			// A resource filter selects decision records whose request named
487			// exactly this resource. Policy-change records never match, even when
488			// a published policy carries the identical ResourceID: the condition
489			// reads the requested resource, not policy content. The comparison is
490			// Go string equality over the stored raw bytes, so case, surrounding
491			// and internal spaces, control bytes and invalid UTF-8 are all
492			// significant, and no path or wildcard is interpreted.
493			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil ||
494				r.Decision.Request.Resource.ID != resourceID {
495				return false
496			}
497		}
498		return true
499	}
500	
501	// optionalResourceCondition extracts the optional resource condition passed
502	// as the trailing variadic argument. An absent argument or an empty string
503	// means "no resource filter"; supplying more than one condition is a caller
504	// error rather than a silently picked value.
505	func optionalResourceCondition(conds []string) (string, error) {
506		switch len(conds) {
507		case 0:
508			return "", nil
509		case 1:
510			return conds[0], nil
511		default:
512			return "", fmt.Errorf("%w: at most one resource condition may be set, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, len(conds))
513		}
514	}
515	
516	// AuditQuery pins the first page of an audit query. startSeq is the first
517	// sequence considered (1 from the beginning); endSeq <= 0 means "everything
518	// currently stored". The returned checkpoint must be passed to AuditPage
519	// for the following pages, so records appended after the first query never
520	// mix into later pages.
521	//
522	// kind and subjectID are the existing optional filters (empty means unset):
523	// kind selects a record category and subjectID selects one subject's
524	// decision records. The optional trailing resourceID adds a resource
525	// condition, empty or absent meaning unset: only decision records whose
526	// requested resource ID equals it byte-for-byte survive — case sensitive,
527	// spaces and control bytes significant, no path or wildcard interpretation,
528	// invalid UTF-8 kept as-is — and policy-change records never survive it,
529	// even when a published policy names the same resource ID. Every set
530	// condition applies together. A resource filter changes only which records
531	// are returned: paging, checkpoints and detached copies behave exactly as
532	// without it, and omitting it preserves the historical call and its results.
533	func (s *Store) AuditQuery(org string, startSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string, resourceID ...string) (*AuditPage, error) {
534		resource, err := optionalResourceCondition(resourceID)
535		if err != nil {
536			return nil, err
537		}
538		if org == "" {
539			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
540		}
541		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
542			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
543		}
544		if pageSize <= 0 {
545			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
546		}
547		if startSeq < 1 {
548			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence must be >= 1, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, startSeq)
549		}
550		s.mu.Lock()
551		defer s.mu.Unlock()
552		st := s.orgLocked(org)
553		end, fingerprint := st.auditHeadLocked(org)
554		cp := Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: end, Fingerprint: fingerprint}
555		if end == 0 {
556			// An organization with no records always yields the empty genesis
557			// page, regardless of where the caller asked to begin.
558			return &AuditPage{Org: org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
559		}
560		if startSeq > end {
561			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: start sequence %d is beyond end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, startSeq, end)
562		}
563		return s.auditPageLocked(org, startSeq, end, fingerprint, pageSize, kind, subjectID, resource), nil
564	}
565	
566	// AuditPage returns one page of a previously pinned query. nextSeq is the
567	// cursor from the previous page; when it is 0 the range is exhausted. The
568	// checkpoint is re-verified against the chain on every call.
569	//
570	// A root checkpoint (EndSeq 0 with the organization's genesis fingerprint)
571	// pins the empty range the organization had when it was issued by a first
572	// AuditQuery or AuditExport. That range is finished independently of what
573	// the store currently holds for the organization: never seen, only queried
574	// empty, or since appended to — the answer is identical. Both terminal
575	// cursors, 0 and the one-past-end cursor 1, return the empty end page with
576	// BeginSeq 1, EndSeq 0 and Next 0; a cursor above 1 is ErrInvalidRange.
577	// Appended records never enter the pinned range; only a fresh AuditQuery
578	// pins the new tail.
579	//
580	// The filters are the same as AuditQuery's and must agree with the pinned
581	// query: pass the same kind, subjectID and optional resourceID on every
582	// page. The resource condition is an exact raw-byte match over requested
583	// resource IDs and excludes policy-change records, exactly as on the first
584	// page; omitting it keeps the historical call and result shape.
585	func (s *Store) AuditPage(cp Checkpoint, nextSeq, pageSize int, kind, subjectID string, resourceID ...string) (*AuditPage, error) {
586		resource, err := optionalResourceCondition(resourceID)
587		if err != nil {
588			return nil, err
589		}
590		if cp.Org == "" {
591			return nil, ErrMissingOrganization
592		}
593		if kind != "" && kind != AuditPolicyChange && kind != AuditDecision {
594			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: unknown category %q", ErrInvalidPage, kind)
595		}
596		if pageSize <= 0 {
597			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: page size must be positive, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, pageSize)
598		}
599		if nextSeq < 0 {
600			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, nextSeq)
601		}
602		if cp.EndSeq < 0 {
603			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
604		}
605		s.mu.Lock()
606		defer s.mu.Unlock()
607		genesis := genesisFingerprint(cp.Org)
608		if cp.EndSeq == 0 {
609			// A root checkpoint pins the empty range the organization had when
610			// it was issued. Read-only paging must never depend on whether this
611			// store happens to have visited the organization since: the chain
612			// state for a never-seen org, an org only queried empty, and an org
613			// that later grew records all answer the same.
614			if cp.Fingerprint != genesis {
615				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the root at sequence 0", ErrInvalidRange)
616			}
617			// Cursor 0 means exhausted; cursor 1 is the one-past-the-end end
618			// page, exactly like EndSeq+1 on a non-empty range — it never
619			// restarts the walk (which is impossible anyway: the pinned range
620			// contains no records). A larger cursor claims positive records the
621			// checkpoint says do not exist, whether or not the live chain now
622			// has them.
623			if nextSeq > 1 {
624				return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence %d beyond pinned empty range ending at 0", ErrInvalidRange, nextSeq)
625			}
626			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: 0, Next: 0, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
627		}
628		st, ok := s.orgs[cp.Org]
629		if !ok {
630			// The checkpoint claims positive records in an organization this
631			// store has never seen; it can never verify.
632			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization has no records", ErrInvalidRange)
633		}
634		head := len(st.audit)
635		if cp.EndSeq > head {
636			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq, head)
637		}
638		wantFP := st.audit[cp.EndSeq-1].Fingerprint
639		if cp.Fingerprint != wantFP {
640			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the chain at sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
641		}
642		if nextSeq == 0 {
643			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: 1, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
644		}
645		if nextSeq > cp.EndSeq+1 {
646			return nil, fmt.Errorf("%w: next sequence %d beyond pinned range ending at %d", ErrInvalidRange, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq)
647		}
648		if nextSeq == cp.EndSeq+1 {
649			return &AuditPage{Org: cp.Org, BeginSeq: nextSeq, EndSeq: cp.EndSeq, Checkpoint: cp}, nil
650		}
651		return s.auditPageLocked(cp.Org, nextSeq, cp.EndSeq, wantFP, pageSize, kind, subjectID, resource), nil
652	}
653	
654	// auditPageLocked scans forward collecting up to pageSize matching records
655	// and computes the next-page cursor. It does not stop at pageSize raw
656	// records: filtering happens within the pinned [start,end] window, so
657	// non-matching records between matches — including policy changes excluded
658	// by a resource condition — never consume page slots.
659	func (s *Store) auditPageLocked(org string, startSeq, endSeq int, endFP string, pageSize int, kind, subjectID, resourceID string) *AuditPage {
660		st := s.orgs[org]
661		// pageSize only bounds how many records this page returns; it must not
662		// drive allocation. A caller may pass any positive value, including the
663		// largest int, for a range holding a handful of records, so preallocate
664		// no more than the window can actually contain.
665		window := endSeq - startSeq + 1
666		capHint := pageSize
667		if window < capHint {
668			capHint = window
669		}
670		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, capHint)
671		i := startSeq
672		for ; i <= endSeq && len(out) < pageSize; i++ {
673			r := st.audit[i-1]
674			if recordMatches(r, kind, subjectID, resourceID) {
675				out = append(out, *cloneRecord(r))
676			}
677		}
678		next := 0
679		if i <= endSeq {
680			next = i
681		}
682		return &AuditPage{
683			Org:        org,
684			Records:    out,
685			BeginSeq:   startSeq,
686			EndSeq:     endSeq,
687			Next:       next,
688			Checkpoint: Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: endFP},
689		}
690	}
691	
692	// AuditExport returns detached copies of the complete records through
693	// endSeq, suitable for offline verification. endSeq <= 0 means everything
694	// currently stored. An organization with no records yields an empty slice
695	// together with its sequence-0 checkpoint.
696	func (s *Store) AuditExport(org string, endSeq int) (records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint, err error) {
697		if org == "" {
698			return nil, Checkpoint{}, ErrMissingOrganization
699		}
700		s.mu.Lock()
701		defer s.mu.Unlock()
702		st := s.orgLocked(org)
703		head := len(st.audit)
704		if endSeq <= 0 {
705			endSeq = head
706		}
707		if endSeq > head {
708			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence %d beyond %d", ErrInvalidRange, endSeq, head)
709		}
710		if endSeq < 0 {
711			return nil, Checkpoint{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: end sequence must be >= 0, got %d", ErrInvalidPage, endSeq)
712		}
713		// The checkpoint fingerprints the final exported record, not the
714		// possibly later current head.
715		fingerprint := genesisFingerprint(org)
716		if endSeq > 0 {
717			fingerprint = st.audit[endSeq-1].Fingerprint
718		}
719		out := make([]AuditRecord, 0, endSeq)
720		for i := 0; i < endSeq; i++ {
721			out = append(out, *cloneRecord(st.audit[i]))
722		}
723		return out, Checkpoint{Org: org, EndSeq: endSeq, Fingerprint: fingerprint}, nil
724	}
725	
726	// VerifyAudit validates an exported record set entirely without a Store.
727	// The caller separately retains the organization, end sequence and
728	// fingerprint they expect. It rejects any modified field, missing middle or
729	// tail record, swapped order, and record spliced in from another
730	// organization. Empty or nil records validate exactly when the checkpoint
731	// is the organization's genesis (end sequence 0).
732	func VerifyAudit(org string, records []AuditRecord, cp Checkpoint) error {
733		if org == "" {
734			return ErrMissingOrganization
735		}
736		if cp.Org != "" && cp.Org != org {
737			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint organization %q does not match %q", ErrInvalidRange, cp.Org, org)
738		}
739		genesis := genesisFingerprint(org)
740		if len(records) == 0 {
741			if cp.EndSeq != 0 || cp.Fingerprint != genesis {
742				return fmt.Errorf("%w: empty records but checkpoint claims end sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, cp.EndSeq)
743			}
744			return nil
745		}
746		if cp.EndSeq != len(records) {
747			return fmt.Errorf("%w: have %d records, checkpoint ends at %d", ErrInvalidRange, len(records), cp.EndSeq)
748		}
749		prev := genesis
750		for i, r := range records {
751			wantSeq := i + 1
752			if r.Org != org {
753				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d belongs to organization %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Org)
754			}
755			if r.Seq != wantSeq {
756				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has sequence %d", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Seq)
757			}
758			if r.PrevFingerprint != prev {
759				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d breaks the chain", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
760			}
761			wantFP := fingerprintFor(&r)
762			if r.Fingerprint != wantFP {
763				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d fingerprint mismatch", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
764			}
765			if r.Kind == AuditPolicyChange {
766				if r.Change == nil || r.Decision != nil {
767					return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d payload does not match its category", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
768				}
769			} else if r.Kind == AuditDecision {
770				if r.Decision == nil || r.Change != nil {
771					return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d payload does not match its category", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq)
772				}
773			} else {
774				return fmt.Errorf("%w: record %d has unknown category %q", ErrInvalidRange, wantSeq, r.Kind)
775			}
776			prev = r.Fingerprint
777		}
778		last := records[len(records)-1]
779		if last.Fingerprint != cp.Fingerprint {
780			return fmt.Errorf("%w: checkpoint fingerprint does not match the final record", ErrInvalidRange)
781		}
782		return nil
783	}
784	
785	// RecheckDecision re-evaluates the request stored in an organization's
786	// decision record against the policy version that decision actually used.
787	// Later publishes or rollbacks cannot alter the result. Non-decision
788	// records and missing sequences return distinguishable errors.
789	//
790	// The record and the version snapshot come exclusively from this
791	// organization's own live history; the version-zero and historical-policy
792	// judgment itself is shared with RecheckDecisionOffline in
793	// replayRecordedDecision.
794	func (s *Store) RecheckDecision(org string, seq int) (Decision, error) {
795		if org == "" {
796			return Decision{}, ErrMissingOrganization
797		}
798		if seq < 1 {
799			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, seq)
800		}
801		s.mu.Lock()
802		defer s.mu.Unlock()
803		st, ok := s.orgs[org]
804		if !ok || seq > len(st.audit) {
805			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: organization %q has no audit sequence %d", ErrAuditNotFound, org, seq)
806		}
807		rec := st.audit[seq-1]
808		if rec.Kind != AuditDecision || rec.Decision == nil {
809			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: sequence %d is %s", ErrAuditNotADecision, seq, rec.Kind)
810		}
811		req := rec.Decision.Request
812		version := rec.Decision.Decision.Version
813		resolve := func(version int) versionPolicies {
814			src, ok := st.versions[version]
815			if !ok {
816				// A decision's version is immutable and never deleted; its
817				// absence indicates store tampering rather than normal
818				// operation.
819				return versionPolicies{status: replayVersionAbsent}
820			}
821			// Live snapshots are immutable; detach anyway so the returned
822			// decision can never share storage with the store.
823			return versionPolicies{policies: append([]Policy(nil), src...)}
824		}
825		d, status := replayRecordedDecision(org, req, version, resolve)
826		if status == replayVersionAbsent {
827			return Decision{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: decision used version %d, which no longer exists", ErrVersionNotFound, version)
828		}
829		return d, nil
830	}

1	// This file is the business regression guard for scope-name isolation in
2	// organization-level access decisions. Only an actual slash ('/', one byte
3	// 0x2F) is a hierarchy separator: every other byte in a scope segment —
4	// Chinese text, spaces, percent-encoded-looking text, even bytes that are
5	// not valid UTF-8 — is ordinary segment name content. Two requests that
6	// agree in organization, enabled subject, action and resource id and differ
7	// ONLY in the resource scope must therefore be decided by their scope's
8	// original bytes. No case folding, trimming, UTF-8 replacement, percent
9	// decoding or string-prefix reading may move an allow or a deny from one
10	// scope name onto a look-alike.
11	//
12	// The guarded rules, all already implemented by scopeMatches, validateScope
13	// and evaluate in org.go:
14	//
15	//   - An exact (non-recursive) policy matches its scope byte for byte and
16	//     nothing else. After one read allow is published, the same-named scope
17	//     is allowed by it alone; a differently cased name, a name with an extra
18	//     space, and a name that only LOOKS identical because a lone 0xFF, a lone
19	//     0xFE and a genuine U+FFFD display alike cannot borrow the allow. With
20	//     no other matching allow the answer is the default denial
21	//     "no matching allow policy", the hit list is empty, and the version is
22	//     still the published version that was evaluated.
23	//   - When each look-alike name carries its own policy, a request hits only
24	//     the policy bearing its own name; another name's deny never enters its
25	//     hit list or verdict. The single byte 0xFF, the single byte 0xFE and a
26	//     real U+FFFD rune stay three distinct scope names.
27	//   - A recursive policy keeps the exact same name comparison and additionally
28	//     covers true descendants: scopes equal to its raw name, or equal to its
29	//     raw name plus a slash plus more segments. A recursive allow on "org/a"
30	//     reaches "org/a/账本" but never "org/ab/账本"; the literal segment text
31	//     "%2F" is not a slash, so "org/a%2F账本" is a sibling, not a descendant.
32	//     Parents whose own name contains spaces or invalid UTF-8 bytes cover only
33	//     descendants formed by appending a slash to that parent's RAW name.
34	//   - Recursive denies obey the identical boundary: a deny that really matches
35	//     still overrides an allow ("matched deny policy", both identifiers kept in
36	//     ascending order, at the evaluated version), while a deny that misses the
37	//     requested scope name cannot affect another scope's access.
38	//   - A request scope containing consecutive slashes is rejected before any
39	//     policy is evaluated — never silently tidied and then matched. The
40	//     explanation is an explicit invalid-scope reason, version 0 and an empty
41	//     hit list, even when a published allow would cover the tidied path.
42	//
43	// All requests below are envelope-valid apart from the deliberately invalid
44	// scopes: the three organizations agree and the subject is enabled with its
45	// id, the resource id and the action present, so every outcome is genuinely
46	// produced by scope matching or the scope legality check, not by another
47	// envelope rule. The audit half pins that every explanation — allow, policy
48	// deny and default deny — survives the chain, historical review and offline
49	// review with its reason, hit identifiers and actual version intact.
50	package darksafe
51	
52	import (
53		"bytes"
54		"encoding/json"
55		"reflect"
56		"strings"
57		"testing"
58	)
59	
60	// Shared fixture: one organization, one enabled subject, one resource id and
61	// one action. Requests differ only in the resource scope.
62	const (
63		scopeNameOrg        = "acme"
64		scopeNameSubjectID  = "svc-ledger-reader"
65		scopeNameResourceID = "ledger-2026"
66		scopeNameAction     = "read"
67	)
68	
69	// scopeRequest builds an envelope-valid organization request carrying the
70	// given resource scope. Subject and resource organizations agree with the
71	// decision organization and the subject is enabled.
72	func scopeRequest(scope string) OrgRequest {
73		return OrgRequest{
74			SubjectOrg:  scopeNameOrg,
75			ResourceOrg: scopeNameOrg,
76			Subject:     Subject{ID: scopeNameSubjectID, Kind: "service"}, // enabled
77			Resource:    Resource{ID: scopeNameResourceID, Scope: scope},
78			Action:      scopeNameAction,
79		}
80	}
81	
82	// scopePolicy builds one policy for the shared subject, action and scope.
83	func scopePolicy(id, scope string, effect Effect, recursive bool) Policy {
84		return Policy{ID: id, Subject: scopeNameSubjectID, Action: scopeNameAction,
85			Scope: scope, Effect: effect, Recursive: recursive}
86	}
87	
88	// wantScopeDecision pins the full four-field explanation: verdict, reason,
89	// exact hit list (order significant; nil and empty both mean "no hits") and
90	// the version actually evaluated.
91	func wantScopeDecision(t *testing.T, got Decision, allowed bool, reason string, matched []string, version int, context string) {
92		t.Helper()
93		if got.Allowed != allowed {
94			t.Fatalf("%s: allowed = %v, want %v; decision = %+v", context, got.Allowed, allowed, got)
95		}
96		if got.Reason != reason {
97			t.Fatalf("%s: reason = %q, want %q; decision = %+v", context, got.Reason, reason, got)
98		}
99		if got.Version != version {
100			t.Fatalf("%s: version = %d, want %d; decision = %+v", context, got.Version, version, got)
101		}
102		gotMatched := got.Matched
103		if len(gotMatched) == 0 {
104			gotMatched = nil
105		}
106		wantMatched := matched
107		if len(wantMatched) == 0 {
108			wantMatched = nil
109		}
110		if !reflect.DeepEqual(gotMatched, wantMatched) {
111			t.Fatalf("%s: matched = %q, want %q; decision = %+v", context, gotMatched, wantMatched, got)
112		}
113	}
114	
115	// TestExactScopeNameGrantsOnlyTheIdenticalScope is the core isolation guard:
116	// one exact read allow published on one scope name admits the same-named
117	// request and no look-alike. Each look-alike is a legal scope (so it reaches
118	// policy evaluation at the published version) but matches nothing, hence the
119	// default denial with an empty hit list at version 1 rather than the allow.
120	func TestExactScopeNameGrantsOnlyTheIdenticalScope(t *testing.T) {
121		exact := "org/账本" // Chinese segment name, valid UTF-8
122		s := NewStore()
123		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
124			scopePolicy("p-exact-allow", exact, EffectAllow, false),
125		})
126		if err != nil || version != 1 {
127			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
128		}
129	
130		// The same-named request hits its own allow and is admitted by it alone.
131		same := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(exact))
132		wantScopeDecision(t, same, true, "matched allow policy",
133			[]string{"p-exact-allow"}, 1, "byte-identical scope")
134	
135		// Every look-alike is a DIFFERENT scope name: it may not borrow the
136		// allow, hits nothing, and falls through to the default denial at the
137		// version actually evaluated. None is an invalid request shape.
138		lookAlikes := map[string]string{
139			"different case in ascii segment": "Org/账本",
140			"extra leading space":             " org/账本",
141			"extra trailing space":            "org/账本 ",
142			"extra space inside the name":     "org/账 本",
143			"extra slash-separated space seg": "org/ /账本",
144		}
145		for name, scope := range lookAlikes {
146			d := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scope))
147			wantScopeDecision(t, d, false, "no matching allow policy",
148				nil, 1, name+" must not match "+showScope(exact))
149		}
150	
151		// The allow really was available: re-deciding the exact scope after the
152		// look-alikes still admits, proving the denials came from name mismatch.
153		again := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(exact))
154		wantScopeDecision(t, again, true, "matched allow policy",
155			[]string{"p-exact-allow"}, 1, "exact scope after look-alike probes")
156	}
157	
158	// rawByteScopes returns the three byte-different-but-display-conflated scope
159	// names used by this file. The path shape is identical and exactly one
160	// segment byte differs: a lone 0xFF, a lone 0xFE, and a genuine U+FFFD code
161	// point (valid UTF-8, the three bytes EF BF BD).
162	func rawByteScopes() (withFF, withFE, withReplacement string) {
163		return "org/账" + invalidByte + "本",
164			"org/账" + anotherInvalidByte + "本",
165			"org/账" + replacementRune + "本"
166	}
167	
168	// TestRawByteScopeNamesStayDistinct guards the display-confusable triple in
169	// the scope path: JSON renders the lone 0xFF and lone 0xFE identically, but
170	// authorization compares raw bytes. With one exact allow on the 0xFF name,
171	// neither the 0xFE name nor the genuine-U+FFFD name (nor the 0xFF name with
172	// an extra space) may be admitted; each gets the default denial at the
173	// evaluated version.
174	func TestRawByteScopeNamesStayDistinct(t *testing.T) {
175		scopeFF, scopeFE, scopeFD := rawByteScopes()
176	
177		// Document the premise: Go distinguishes all three, while encoding/json
178		// collapses the two lone invalid bytes to one rendering. Any matching
179		// layer that normalized before comparing would fail this regression.
180		if scopeFF == scopeFE || scopeFF == scopeFD || scopeFE == scopeFD {
181			t.Fatalf("test premise broken: scopes must differ pairwise: %q %q %q", scopeFF, scopeFE, scopeFD)
182		}
183		jFF, _ := json.Marshal(scopeFF)
184		jFE, _ := json.Marshal(scopeFE)
185		if !bytes.Equal(jFF, jFE) {
186			t.Fatalf("test premise broken: JSON renders the invalid bytes differently: %s vs %s", jFF, jFE)
187		}
188	
189		s := NewStore()
190		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
191			scopePolicy("p-scope-ff-allow", scopeFF, EffectAllow, false),
192		})
193		if err != nil || version != 1 {
194			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
195		}
196	
197		allowFF := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scopeFF))
198		wantScopeDecision(t, allowFF, true, "matched allow policy",
199			[]string{"p-scope-ff-allow"}, 1, "0xFF scope hits its own allow")
200	
201		// The look-alikes are legal scopes that match nothing: default denial,
202		// empty hit list, but still evaluated at published version 1 — never an
203		// envelope rejection and never the 0xFF allow.
204		lookAlikes := map[string]string{
205			"lone 0xFE look-alike":          scopeFE,
206			"genuine U+FFFD look-alike":     scopeFD,
207			"0xFF name with a trailing sp.": scopeFF + " ",
208			"0xFF name with a leading sp.":  " " + scopeFF,
209		}
210		for name, scope := range lookAlikes {
211			d := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scope))
212			wantScopeDecision(t, d, false, "no matching allow policy",
213				nil, 1, name)
214			for _, hit := range d.Matched {
215				if hit == "p-scope-ff-allow" {
216					t.Fatalf("%s borrowed the 0xFF allow: %+v", name, d)
217				}
218			}
219		}
220	}
221	
222	// TestEachScopeNameHitsOnlyItsOwnPolicy publishes one policy per look-alike
223	// name in a single version and proves requests cannot cross names. The 0xFF
224	// name allows, the 0xFE name denies and the genuine-U+FFFD name also allows:
225	// each request must hit its own identifier and its own effect alone. The
226	// 0xFE deny in particular must never be reported on either of the other two
227	// requests.
228	func TestEachScopeNameHitsOnlyItsOwnPolicy(t *testing.T) {
229		scopeFF, scopeFE, scopeFD := rawByteScopes()
230		s := NewStore()
231		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
232			scopePolicy("p-scope-ff-allow", scopeFF, EffectAllow, false),
233			scopePolicy("p-scope-fe-deny", scopeFE, EffectDeny, false),
234			scopePolicy("p-scope-fd-allow", scopeFD, EffectAllow, false),
235		})
236		if err != nil || version != 1 {
237			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
238		}
239	
240		dFF := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scopeFF))
241		wantScopeDecision(t, dFF, true, "matched allow policy",
242			[]string{"p-scope-ff-allow"}, 1, "0xFF scope hits only its own allow")
243	
244		dFE := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scopeFE))
245		wantScopeDecision(t, dFE, false, "matched deny policy",
246			[]string{"p-scope-fe-deny"}, 1, "0xFE scope hits only its own deny")
247	
248		dFD := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scopeFD))
249		wantScopeDecision(t, dFD, true, "matched allow policy",
250			[]string{"p-scope-fd-allow"}, 1, "U+FFFD scope hits only its own allow")
251	
252		// A fourth, unlisted but legal name gets the default denial and must not
253		// pick up ANY of the three identifiers — especially not the 0xFE deny.
254		unlisted := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest("org/账"+replacementRune+"目"))
255		wantScopeDecision(t, unlisted, false, "no matching allow policy",
256			nil, 1, "unlisted scope borrows no policy")
257	}
258	
259	// TestRecursiveScopeCoversRealDescendantsOnly pins the recursive boundary
260	// using raw, byte-exact parent names. A recursive allow on "org/a":
261	//
262	//   - covers the parent itself and a true child carrying a Chinese segment;
263	//   - does not cover a same-prefix sibling segment ("org/ab/账本"), since only
264	//     a real slash starts a child segment;
265	//   - does not cover "org/a%2F账本": "%2F" is three literal characters in a
266	//     segment name, never decoded into a slash.
267	func TestRecursiveScopeCoversRealDescendantsOnly(t *testing.T) {
268		parent := "org/a"
269		s := NewStore()
270		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
271			scopePolicy("p-rec-allow", parent, EffectAllow, true),
272		})
273		if err != nil || version != 1 {
274			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
275		}
276	
277		covered := map[string]string{
278			"parent itself":     parent,
279			"chinese child":     "org/a/账本",
280			"deeper descendant": "org/a/账本/明细",
281			"child with spaces": "org/a/账 本 ",
282		}
283		for name, scope := range covered {
284			d := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scope))
285			wantScopeDecision(t, d, true, "matched allow policy",
286				[]string{"p-rec-allow"}, 1, name)
287		}

289		notCovered := map[string]string{
290			"sibling prefix segment": "org/ab/账本",
291			"literal %2F in segment": "org/a%2F账本",
292			"percent-encoded deeper": "org/a%2F账本/明细",
293			"ancestor":               "org",
294			"space-padded lookalike": "org/a /账本",
295			"uppercase lookalike":    "org/A/账本",
296		}
297		for name, scope := range notCovered {
298			d := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scope))
299			wantScopeDecision(t, d, false, "no matching allow policy",
300				nil, 1, name)
301		}

304	// TestRecursiveParentWithSpacesOrRawBytesOnlyCoversRawChildren proves the
305	// descendant prefix is the parent's RAW name plus a slash, even when the
306	// parent name itself contains spaces or invalid UTF-8 bytes. A child formed
307	// by appending a slash to a display-alike name is outside the subtree.
308	func TestRecursiveParentWithSpacesOrRawBytesOnlyCoversRawChildren(t *testing.T) {
309		spacedParent := "org/账 本"
310		rawParent := "org/账" + invalidByte + "本"
311	
312		cases := []struct {
313			name    string
314			parent  string
315			child   string
316			outside []string
317		}{
318			{
319				name:   "parent name contains a space",
320				parent: spacedParent,
321				child:  spacedParent + "/明细",
322				outside: []string{
323					"org/账/本/明细",                       // space reinterpreted as a slash is not allowed
324					"org/账 本x/明细",                      // one extra byte in the segment
325					"org/账 本 /明细",                      // trailing space before the separator
326					"org/账%20本/明细",                     // literal %20, not the space
327					"org/账" + replacementRune + "本/明细", // U+FFFD, not the space
328				},
329			},
330			{
331				name:   "parent name contains a lone 0xFF byte",
332				parent: rawParent,
333				child:  rawParent + "/明细",
334				outside: []string{
335					"org/账" + anotherInvalidByte + "本/明细", // 0xFE parent prefix
336					"org/账" + replacementRune + "本/明细",    // genuine U+FFFD prefix
337					"org/账" + invalidByte + "本x/明细",       // longer raw segment
338				},
339			},
340		}
341		for _, tc := range cases {
342			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
343				s := NewStore()
344				version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
345					scopePolicy("p-rec-raw", tc.parent, EffectAllow, true),
346				})
347				if err != nil || version != 1 {
348					t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
349				}
350	
351				atParent := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(tc.parent))
352				wantScopeDecision(t, atParent, true, "matched allow policy",
353					[]string{"p-rec-raw"}, 1, "read at the raw parent itself")
354	
355				child := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(tc.child))
356				wantScopeDecision(t, child, true, "matched allow policy",
357					[]string{"p-rec-raw"}, 1, "child formed by raw parent name plus a slash")
358	
359				for _, scope := range tc.outside {
360					d := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scope))
361					wantScopeDecision(t, d, false, "no matching allow policy",
362						nil, 1, "outside subtree: "+showScope(scope))
363				}
364			})
365		}
366	}

368	// TestRecursiveDenyBoundaryIsByteExact verifies recursive denies under the
369	// same name rules. A recursive deny that really covers the request still
370	// overrides an exact allow on the child, with BOTH identifiers kept in
371	// ascending order at the evaluated version. But a recursive deny on a
372	// look-alike parent — org/a rather than org/a%2F账本's true parent, or a
373	// parent whose name carries 0xFE where the request carries 0xFF — does not
374	// match and cannot change the other scope's allow.
375	func TestRecursiveDenyBoundaryIsByteExact(t *testing.T) {
376		// Real conflict: recursive deny on org/a covers org/a/账本 even though an
377		// exact allow sits on the child.
378		s := NewStore()
379		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
380			scopePolicy("a-child-allow", "org/a/账本", EffectAllow, false),
381			scopePolicy("z-parent-deny", "org/a", EffectDeny, true),
382		})
383		if err != nil || version != 1 {
384			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
385		}
386		conflict := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest("org/a/账本"))
387		wantScopeDecision(t, conflict, false, "matched deny policy",
388			[]string{"a-child-allow", "z-parent-deny"}, 1, "real recursive deny overrides child allow")
389	
390		// Submission order must not move the explanation.
391		s2 := NewStore()
392		if v, err := s2.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
393			scopePolicy("z-parent-deny", "org/a", EffectDeny, true),
394			scopePolicy("a-child-allow", "org/a/账本", EffectAllow, false),
395		}); err != nil || v != 1 {
396			t.Fatalf("reordered publish = %d, %v", v, err)
397		}
398		reordered := s2.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest("org/a/账本"))
399		if !reflect.DeepEqual(reordered, conflict) {
400			t.Fatalf("policy submission order changed the decision:\n%+v\n%+v", conflict, reordered)
401		}
402	
403		// Same-prefix miss: the deny on org/a must not reach org/ab/账本. The
404		// sibling scope's own exact allow stands alone.
405		s3 := NewStore()
406		if v, err := s3.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
407			scopePolicy("z-parent-deny", "org/a", EffectDeny, true),
408			scopePolicy("ab-exact-allow", "org/ab/账本", EffectAllow, false),
409		}); err != nil || v != 1 {
410			t.Fatalf("sibling publish = %d, %v", v, err)
411		}
412		sibling := s3.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest("org/ab/账本"))
413		wantScopeDecision(t, sibling, true, "matched allow policy",
414			[]string{"ab-exact-allow"}, 1, "recursive deny on org/a misses org/ab")
415	
416		// Literal-%2F miss: org/a%2F账本 is not under org/a, so its own allow
417		// cannot be overridden by the org/a recursive deny.
418		s4 := NewStore()
419		if v, err := s4.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
420			scopePolicy("z-parent-deny", "org/a", EffectDeny, true),
421			scopePolicy("enc-exact-allow", "org/a%2F账本", EffectAllow, false),
422		}); err != nil || v != 1 {
423			t.Fatalf("encoded publish = %d, %v", v, err)
424		}
425		encoded := s4.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest("org/a%2F账本"))
426		wantScopeDecision(t, encoded, true, "matched allow policy",
427			[]string{"enc-exact-allow"}, 1, "literal %2F scope is outside org/a's deny subtree")
428	
429		// Raw-byte miss: a recursive deny whose parent carries 0xFE must not reach
430		// a child of the genuinely-different 0xFF-named parent.
431		scopeFF, scopeFE, _ := rawByteScopes()
432		s5 := NewStore()
433		if v, err := s5.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
434			scopePolicy("rec-deny-fe", scopeFE, EffectDeny, true),
435			scopePolicy("child-allow-ff", scopeFF+"/明细", EffectAllow, false),
436		}); err != nil || v != 1 {
437			t.Fatalf("raw-byte publish = %d, %v", v, err)
438		}
439		rawChild := s5.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(scopeFF+"/明细"))
440		wantScopeDecision(t, rawChild, true, "matched allow policy",
441			[]string{"child-allow-ff"}, 1, "0xFE recursive deny misses the 0xFF subtree")
442	}

444	// TestConsecutiveSlashScopeRejectedBeforePolicyEvaluation guards the
445	// legality gate: consecutive slashes make a request scope illegal and the
446	// request is denied before policy evaluation, with an explicit invalid-scope
447	// reason, version 0 and an empty hit list. The path must not be tidied and
448	// then matched against the published allow that covers the normalized form.
449	func TestConsecutiveSlashScopeRejectedBeforePolicyEvaluation(t *testing.T) {
450		s := NewStore()
451		// An allow that WOULD cover every normalized form used below, proving the
452		// rejection happens before it could be consulted.
453		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
454			scopePolicy("p-wide-allow", "org/a", EffectAllow, true),
455			scopePolicy("p-ledger-allow", "org/a/账本", EffectAllow, false),
456		})
457		if err != nil || version != 1 {
458			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
459		}
460	
461		illegal := []struct {
462			name  string
463			scope string
464		}{
465			{"double slash in the middle", "org//a/账本"},
466			{"double slash before leaf", "org/a//账本"},
467			{"triple slash", "org///a"},
468			{"leading slash", "/org/a/账本"},
469			{"trailing slash", "org/a/账本/"},
470			{"only slashes", "//"},
471		}
472		for _, tc := range illegal {
473			d := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(tc.scope))
474			if d.Allowed {
475				t.Fatalf("%s: request was allowed after tidying: %+v", tc.name, d)
476			}
477			if d.Version != 0 {
478				t.Fatalf("%s: version = %d, want 0 (no published version may be used); decision = %+v",
479					tc.name, d.Version, d)
480			}
481			if len(d.Matched) != 0 {
482				t.Fatalf("%s: matched = %q, want no policy hits before evaluation", tc.name, d.Matched)
483			}
484			if !strings.HasPrefix(d.Reason, "invalid scope") {
485				t.Fatalf("%s: reason = %q, want an invalid-scope rejection", tc.name, d.Reason)
486			}
487			namesConsecutive := strings.Contains(d.Reason, "consecutive slashes")
488			namesLeadingTrailing := strings.Contains(d.Reason, "leading or trailing slash")
489			if !namesConsecutive && !namesLeadingTrailing {
490				t.Fatalf("%s: reason = %q, must name consecutive or leading/trailing slashes", tc.name, d.Reason)
491			}
492		}
493	
494		// The legal form the illegal scopes would have normalized to is genuinely
495		// covered, proving the denials above come from the legality gate and not
496		// from a missing allow.
497		legal := s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest("org/a/账本"))
498		wantScopeDecision(t, legal, true, "matched allow policy",
499			[]string{"p-ledger-allow", "p-wide-allow"}, 1, "the un-tidied legal scope is covered")
500	}
501	
502	// TestInvalidScopePolicyCannotBePublished mirrors the request gate on the
503	// publishing side: a policy whose scope contains consecutive slashes cannot
504	// enter any published version, so no later decision can ever match one.
505	func TestInvalidScopePolicyCannotBePublished(t *testing.T) {
506		s := NewStore()
507		if v, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, nil); err != nil || v != 1 {
508			t.Fatalf("baseline publish = %d, %v", v, err)
509		}
510		_, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 1, []Policy{
511			scopePolicy("p-bad", "org//a", EffectAllow, false),
512		})
513		if err == nil {
514			t.Fatal("policy with consecutive slashes must fail validation")
515		}
516		if !errorContains(err, "consecutive slashes") {
517			t.Fatalf("err = %v, want it to name consecutive slashes", err)
518		}
519		if got := s.CurrentVersion(scopeNameOrg); got != 1 {
520			t.Fatalf("current version = %d, want 1 after rejected publish", got)
521		}
522	}
523	
524	// errorContains is a small strings.Contains on err's text kept local so the
525	// suite does not add an import just for one assertion.
526	func errorContains(err error, sub string) bool {
527		return err != nil && strings.Contains(err.Error(), sub)
528	}

530	// TestScopeNameDecisionsSurviveReviewAndAudit pins that the full explanation
531	// produced by raw-byte scope matching — allow, policy deny and default deny —
532	// is preserved with reason, hit identifiers and actual version through the
533	// audit record, historical review, online recheck and offline review. The
534	// three display-confusable scopes must also stay pairwise distinguishable in
535	// the signed material rather than collapse onto one replacement character.
536	func TestScopeNameDecisionsSurviveReviewAndAudit(t *testing.T) {
537		scopeFF, scopeFE, scopeFD := rawByteScopes()
538		s := NewStore()
539		version, err := s.Publish(scopeNameOrg, 0, []Policy{
540			scopePolicy("p-scope-ff-allow", scopeFF, EffectAllow, false),
541			scopePolicy("p-scope-fe-deny", scopeFE, EffectDeny, true),
542			scopePolicy("p-scope-fd-allow", scopeFD, EffectAllow, false),
543		})
544		if err != nil || version != 1 {
545			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
546		}
547	
548		// Chain layout (seq 1 is the publish), one decision per distinguished
549		// outcome:
550		//	seq 2  0xFF scope              allow
551		//	seq 3  0xFE scope              deny (recursive deny covers itself)
552		//	seq 4  genuine U+FFFD scope    allow
553		//	seq 5  unlisted raw-byte name  default deny, empty hit list, version 1
554		//	seq 6  "org//a" illegal scope  envelope denial, version 0, no hits
555		unlistedScope := "org/账" + invalidByte + "目"
556		// Decisions must be made in a fixed order: the audit chain assigns its
557		// gapless sequence numbers by Decide call order, not by these keys.
558		seqScopes := []struct {
559			seq   int
560			scope string
561		}{
562			{2, scopeFF}, {3, scopeFE}, {4, scopeFD}, {5, unlistedScope}, {6, "org//a"},
563		}
564		scopesAtSeq := make(map[int]string, len(seqScopes))
565		online := map[int]Decision{}
566		for _, item := range seqScopes {
567			scopesAtSeq[item.seq] = item.scope
568			online[item.seq] = s.Decide(scopeNameOrg, scopeRequest(item.scope))
569		}
570	
571		wantScopeDecision(t, online[2], true, "matched allow policy",
572			[]string{"p-scope-ff-allow"}, 1, "seq 2")
573		wantScopeDecision(t, online[3], false, "matched deny policy",
574			[]string{"p-scope-fe-deny"}, 1, "seq 3")
575		wantScopeDecision(t, online[4], true, "matched allow policy",
576			[]string{"p-scope-fd-allow"}, 1, "seq 4")
577		wantScopeDecision(t, online[5], false, "no matching allow policy",
578			nil, 1, "seq 5 default deny keeps version 1")
579		if d6 := online[6]; d6.Allowed || d6.Version != 0 || len(d6.Matched) != 0 ||
580			!strings.HasPrefix(d6.Reason, "invalid scope") {
581			t.Fatalf("seq 6 illegal scope = %+v, want version-0 invalid-scope denial with no hits", d6)
582		}
583	
584		recs, cp, err := s.AuditExport(scopeNameOrg, 0)
585		if err != nil {
586			t.Fatal(err)
587		}
588		if len(recs) != 6 {
589			t.Fatalf("chain length = %d, want 6 (one publish + five decisions)", len(recs))
590		}
591		if err := VerifyAudit(scopeNameOrg, recs, cp); err != nil {
592			t.Fatalf("raw-byte scope chain must verify: %v", err)
593		}
594	
595		// Each record stores the submitted scope bytes and the returned decision
596		// in full; distinct scope names must not collapse in signed material.
597		for seq, wantScope := range scopesAtSeq {
598			r := recs[seq-1]
599			if r.Kind != AuditDecision || r.Decision == nil {
600				t.Fatalf("seq %d is not a decision record: %+v", seq, r)
601			}
602			if r.Decision.Request.Resource.Scope != wantScope {
603				t.Fatalf("seq %d stored scope %q, want byte-exact %q", seq,
604					r.Decision.Request.Resource.Scope, wantScope)
605			}
606			if !reflect.DeepEqual(r.Decision.Decision, online[seq]) {
607				t.Fatalf("seq %d stored decision %+v != returned %+v",
608					seq, r.Decision.Decision, online[seq])
609			}
610		}
611		fps := map[string]int{}
612		for _, seq := range []int{2, 3, 4} {
613			fp := recs[seq-1].Fingerprint
614			if other, dup := fps[fp]; dup {
615				t.Fatalf("seqs %d and %d share fingerprint %s: confusable scopes collapsed", other, seq, fp)
616			}
617			fps[fp] = seq
618		}
619	
620		// Historical review against version 1 reproduces every explanation, and
621		// review of the illegal scope still rejects at the envelope with
622		// version 0 and no hits — review never tidies before evaluating either.
623		for seq, wantScope := range scopesAtSeq {
624			reviewed := s.Review(scopeNameOrg, version, scopeRequest(wantScope))
625			if !reflect.DeepEqual(reviewed, online[seq]) {
626				t.Fatalf("seq %d (scope %q) review %+v != online %+v",
627					seq, wantScope, reviewed, online[seq])
628			}
629		}
630	
631		// Online recheck replays from the recorded material, including the
632		// default deny (version 1, empty hit list) and the envelope denial.
633		for seq := range scopesAtSeq {
634			replayed, err := s.RecheckDecision(scopeNameOrg, seq)
635			if err != nil {
636				t.Fatalf("RecheckDecision seq %d: %v", seq, err)
637			}
638			if !reflect.DeepEqual(replayed, online[seq]) {
639				t.Fatalf("seq %d recheck %+v != recorded %+v", seq, replayed, online[seq])
640			}
641		}
642	
643		// Offline review over the chain-validated export recomputes each decision
644		// from the saved raw scope and the recorded version, marked consistent.
645		for seq := range scopesAtSeq {
646			review, err := RecheckDecisionOffline(scopeNameOrg, recs, cp, seq)
647			if err != nil {
648				t.Fatalf("offline review seq %d: %v", seq, err)
649			}
650			if !review.Consistent {
651				t.Fatalf("seq %d offline review inconsistent: original %+v vs recomputed %+v",
652					seq, review.Original, review.Recomputed)
653			}
654			if !reflect.DeepEqual(review.Recomputed, online[seq]) {
655				t.Fatalf("seq %d recomputed %+v != online %+v",
656					seq, review.Recomputed, online[seq])
657			}
658		}
659	}

661	// showScope renders a scope for failure messages without relying on its
662	// displayed form, since the confusable bytes all render alike.
663	func showScope(scope string) string {
664		return strings.ReplaceAll(strings.ReplaceAll(scope, invalidByte, `<FF>`), anotherInvalidByte, `<FE>`)
665	}

1	// This file is the regression guard pinning down that the two access entry
2	// points use two different authorization bases:
3	//
4	//   - Access (the demo core) decides solely from the subject's carried
5	//     roles: "owner" or "<scope>:<action>" grants. It never consults a
6	//     published policy, has no policy store, and reports the granting role
7	//     name in Decision.Matched with Version always 0.
8	//   - Store.Decide decides solely from the decision organization's currently
9	//     published policies. Subject roles, even "owner", never participate;
10	//     Decision.Matched carries policy identifiers and Version is the
11	//     published version actually evaluated (0 only when none was used).
12	//
13	// The two legitimately disagree about the same enabled service principal
14	// reading the same ledger, so every assertion below compares the full
15	// explanation — allowed, reason, matched entries and version — never the
16	// boolean alone. All material is generated in-process; the suite needs only
17	// the Go standard library and runs offline.
18	package darksafe
19	
20	import (
21		"reflect"
22		"testing"
23	)
24	
25	// Fixture values shared with examples/org_decision: one enabled service
26	// principal reading one ledger in one organization.
27	const (
28		basisOrg        = "acme factory"
29		basisLedgerID   = "ledger-2026"
30		basisScope      = "acme/factory/ledger"
31		basisSubjectID  = "svc-audit-reader"
32		basisAction     = "read"
33		basisPolicyID   = "p-ledger-read-2026"
34		basisOwnerRole  = "owner"
35		basisScopedRole = basisScope + ":" + basisAction // acme/factory/ledger:read
36	)
37	
38	// basisSubject builds the enabled service principal with the given roles.
39	// No argument means no roles at all.
40	func basisSubject(roles ...string) Subject {
41		return Subject{ID: basisSubjectID, Kind: "service", Roles: roles}
42	}
43	
44	func basisLedger() Resource { return Resource{ID: basisLedgerID, Scope: basisScope} }
45	
46	// basisRequest builds a complete, envelope-valid organization request:
47	// subject organization, resource organization and decision organization all
48	// agree and every identifier and the action are present.
49	func basisRequest(roles ...string) OrgRequest {
50		return OrgRequest{
51			SubjectOrg:  basisOrg,
52			ResourceOrg: basisOrg,
53			Subject:     basisSubject(roles...),
54			Resource:    basisLedger(),
55			Action:      basisAction,
56		}
57	}
58	
59	// basisAllowPolicy is the one matching allow policy: this subject, this
60	// action and the ledger's exact scope, with no resource qualifier.
61	func basisAllowPolicy() Policy {
62		return allowPolicy(basisPolicyID, basisSubjectID, basisAction, basisScope, false)
63	}
64	
65	// wantDecision compares the complete explanation an entry point must
66	// preserve. Matched order is significant (policy hits are documented as
67	// sorted); a nil list and a non-nil empty list are the same explanation,
68	// namely "nothing matched".
69	func wantDecision(t *testing.T, got Decision, allowed bool, reason string, matched []string, version int, context string) {
70		t.Helper()
71		if got.Allowed != allowed {
72			t.Fatalf("%s: allowed = %v, want %v; decision = %+v", context, got.Allowed, allowed, got)
73		}
74		if got.Reason != reason {
75			t.Fatalf("%s: reason = %q, want %q; decision = %+v", context, got.Reason, reason, got)
76		}
77		if got.Version != version {
78			t.Fatalf("%s: version = %d, want %d; decision = %+v", context, got.Version, version, got)
79		}
80		gotMatched := got.Matched
81		if len(gotMatched) == 0 {
82			gotMatched = nil
83		}
84		wantMatched := matched
85		if len(wantMatched) == 0 {
86			wantMatched = nil
87		}
88		if !reflect.DeepEqual(gotMatched, wantMatched) {
89			t.Fatalf("%s: matched = %q, want %q; decision = %+v", context, gotMatched, wantMatched, got)
90		}

93	// TestAccessAndDecideUseDifferentAuthorizationBases drives the same enabled
94	// principal and ledger through both entry points before any policy is
95	// published. Access allows on a role while Decide denies for lack of a
96	// published version: the divergence is expected, and the two sides'
97	// explanations must not be read as the same kind of grant.
98	func TestAccessAndDecideUseDifferentAuthorizationBases(t *testing.T) {
99		cases := []struct {
100			name  string
101			roles []string
102			grant string // the role that actually grants the Access read
103		}{
104			{name: "owner role", roles: []string{basisOwnerRole}, grant: basisOwnerRole},
105			{name: "ledger scoped read role", roles: []string{basisScopedRole}, grant: basisScopedRole},
106		}
107		for _, tc := range cases {
108			t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
109				subject := basisSubject(tc.roles...)
110	
111				// Access: the carried role is the whole authorization basis. The
112				// matched entry is the role that actually granted the read, and
113				// version 0 means Access never evaluates a published policy.
114				access := Access(subject, basisLedger(), basisAction)
115				wantDecision(t, access,
116					true, "role grants "+basisAction+":"+basisScope,
117					[]string{tc.grant}, 0, "Access with granting role")
118	
119				// Decide on a fresh store: the envelope is valid (all three
120				// organizations agree, identifiers complete) and the very same
121				// roles ride along in the request, but no policy has been
122				// published. Roles cannot stand in for one, so the request is
123				// denied, the reason names the missing published version, the
124				// matched list is empty and no version was used.
125				store := NewStore()
126				decide := store.Decide(basisOrg, basisRequest(tc.roles...))
127				wantDecision(t, decide,
128					false, "organization has no published version",
129					nil, 0, "Decide before first publish")
130	
131				// The two version-0 answers are not one shared record: Access
132				// allowed carrying a role name, Decide denied with an empty hit
133				// list. A role name must never be reported as an org policy hit.
134				if len(decide.Matched) != 0 {
135					t.Fatalf("unpublished Decide must have no matched entries, got %q", decide.Matched)
136				}
137				if reflect.DeepEqual(access.Matched, decide.Matched) {
138					t.Fatalf("Access role hit %q must not be interpretable as a Decide policy hit", access.Matched)
139				}
140			})
141		}
142	}

268	// TestChangingRolesNeverChangesOrgDecision varies only the carried roles.
269	// As long as the request content and published policy are otherwise
270	// unchanged, the organization decision must be identical in every
271	// explanatory field — not just in whether it allows. Meanwhile the demo
272	// decision does vary with the roles, proving the inputs are meaningful.
273	func TestChangingRolesNeverChangesOrgDecision(t *testing.T) {
274		store := NewStore()
275		version, err := store.Publish(basisOrg, 0, []Policy{basisAllowPolicy()})
276		if err != nil || version != 1 {
277			t.Fatalf("publish matching allow = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
278		}
279	
280		roleSets := [][]string{
281			nil,
282			{},
283			{basisOwnerRole},
284			{basisScopedRole},
285			{basisOwnerRole, basisScopedRole},
286			{basisScopedRole, basisOwnerRole},
287			{"unrelated-role", "admin"},
288			{basisScope + ":write"}, // a write role says nothing about the read
289		}
290	
291		baseline := store.Decide(basisOrg, basisRequest(roleSets[0]...))
292		wantDecision(t, baseline, true, "matched allow policy",
293			[]string{basisPolicyID}, version, "baseline org decision")
294	
295		sawAccessAllow, sawAccessDeny := false, false
296		for _, roles := range roleSets {
297			context := "role variant " + describeRoles(roles)
298			got := store.Decide(basisOrg, basisRequest(roles...))
299			// Full-field pinning: allowed, reason, matched list (and order) and
300			// version all stay constant as the roles change.
301			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, baseline) {
302				t.Fatalf("%s: org decision changed from %+v to %+v", context, baseline, got)
303			}
304			if got.Allowed && (len(got.Matched) != 1 || got.Matched[0] != basisPolicyID) {
305				t.Fatalf("%s: allow must be attributed to the policy, not roles: %+v", context, got)
306			}
307	
308			access := Access(basisSubject(roles...), basisLedger(), basisAction)
309			if access.Allowed {
310				sawAccessAllow = true
311				wantDecision(t, access, true, "role grants "+basisAction+":"+basisScope,
312					rolesContainingGrant(roles), 0, context+" Access")
313			} else {
314				sawAccessDeny = true
315				wantDecision(t, access, false, "no role grants "+basisAction+":"+basisScope,
316					nil, 0, context+" Access")
317			}
318		}
319		if !sawAccessAllow || !sawAccessDeny {
320			t.Fatalf("role variants must move the demo decision both ways, saw allow=%v deny=%v",
321				sawAccessAllow, sawAccessDeny)
322		}
323	}

325	// describeRoles renders a role set for test failure messages.
326	func describeRoles(roles []string) string {
327		if roles == nil {
328			return "<nil>"
329		}
330		return "[" + joinRoles(roles) + "]"
331	}
332	
333	func joinRoles(roles []string) string {
334		out := ""
335		for i, r := range roles {
336			if i > 0 {
337				out += ","
338			}
339			out += r
340		}
341		return out
342	}

344	// rolesContainingGrant returns the role that Access actually grants with,
345	// in iteration order, for an Access allow assertion.
346	func rolesContainingGrant(roles []string) []string {
347		for _, r := range roles {
348			if r == basisOwnerRole || r == basisScopedRole {
349				return []string{r}
350			}
351		}
352		return nil
353	}

415	// the unpublished-version denial, the disabled-subject denial and both
416	// organization-mismatch denials — appends exactly one decision record whose

421	
422		noPolicy := store.Decide(basisOrg, basisRequest(basisOwnerRole)) // seq 1: denial, version 0
423		wantDecision(t, noPolicy, false, "organization has no published version", nil, 0,
424			"recorded unpublished denial")

427		if err != nil || version != 1 {
428			t.Fatalf("publish = %d, %v; want 1, nil", version, err)
429		}
430	
431		allowedNoRoles := store.Decide(basisOrg, basisRequest()) // seq 3: policy allow, version 1
432		wantDecision(t, allowedNoRoles, true, "matched allow policy",
433			[]string{basisPolicyID}, 1, "recorded allow")
434	
435		disabled := basisRequest(basisOwnerRole)
436		disabled.Subject.Disabled = true
437		disabledDenial := store.Decide(basisOrg, disabled) // seq 4: envelope denial
438		wantDecision(t, disabledDenial, false, "subject is disabled", nil, 0, "recorded disabled denial")
439

441		subjectMismatch.SubjectOrg = "globex"
442		mismatchDenial := store.Decide(basisOrg, subjectMismatch) // seq 5
443		wantDecision(t, mismatchDenial, false, "organization mismatch", nil, 0,
444			"recorded subject-org mismatch denial")
445	
446		resourceMismatch := basisRequest(basisScopedRole)
447		resourceMismatch.ResourceOrg = "globex"
448		resourceMismatchDenial := store.Decide(basisOrg, resourceMismatch) // seq 6
449		wantDecision(t, resourceMismatchDenial, false, "organization mismatch", nil, 0,
450			"recorded resource-org mismatch denial")
451	
452		records, cp, err := store.AuditExport(basisOrg, 0)
453		if err != nil {
454			t.Fatalf("AuditExport: %v", err)
455		}
456		if len(records) != 6 {
457			t.Fatalf("chain length = %d, want 6 (one publish + five decisions)", len(records))
458		}
459		if err := VerifyAudit(basisOrg, records, cp); err != nil {
460			t.Fatalf("decision chain must verify including every denial: %v", err)
461		}

463		for i := range records {
464			if records[i].Seq != i+1 {
465				t.Fatalf("record %d has seq %d, want gapless %d", i, records[i].Seq, i+1)
466			}
467		}
468	
469		// The single policy change sits at seq 2; every other record is a
470		// decision carrying the exact returned conclusion and submitted request.
471		change := records[1]

473			t.Fatalf("seq 2 must be the version-1 policy change: %+v", change)
474		}
475	
476		type recorded struct {
477			seq      int
478			decision Decision
479			request  OrgRequest
480		}
481		want := []recorded{
482			{seq: 1, decision: noPolicy, request: basisRequest(basisOwnerRole)},
483			{seq: 3, decision: allowedNoRoles, request: basisRequest()},
484			{seq: 4, decision: disabledDenial, request: disabled},
485			{seq: 5, decision: mismatchDenial, request: subjectMismatch},
486			{seq: 6, decision: resourceMismatchDenial, request: resourceMismatch},
487		}
488		for _, w := range want {

491				t.Fatalf("seq %d is not a decision record: %+v", w.seq, r)
492			}
493			// The recorded conclusion matches the returned one field for field,

495			if !reflect.DeepEqual(r.Decision.Decision, w.decision) {
496				t.Fatalf("seq %d recorded decision %+v != returned %+v",

513		}

515		// Concretely, the version-0 denial records really carry empty hit lists
